## Who Erodes Democracy? Actor-Level Evidence from a Two-Part Model of Authoritarian Behavior

**Emily McKay** · Faculty mentor: Prof. Maria Popova · American University, 2026

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Session winner, "Justice, Equality, & Power,"** 18th Annual Undergraduate Research Symposium, American University, April 2026.
:::

Democratic backsliding is usually pinned on strongmen. This paper asks **which institutions' authoritarian actions actually predict democratic decline**. I merged 23,421 hand-coded events from the Democratic Erosion Event Dataset with V-Dem democracy scores. Then I used two-part fixed-effects panel models to separate the *onset* of authoritarian behaviour by an institution from its *escalation*.

**Main findings:** the military, police, judiciary and ruling party each predict decline independently of the head of state. The first authoritarian action by a new institution is a stronger warning sign than further actions by one already involved. Sustained civil-society and international engagement are associated with resilience.

### Work in progress

**Spatial contagion of democratic backsliding.** Do authoritarian events in neighbouring countries predict later democratic decline at home? This extension uses a contiguity-weighted spatial lag of DEED events and draws on theories of demonstration effects.
